{{Short description|Detention center in Florida, US}}
{{Use American English|date=August 2025}}
The '''Glades County Detention Center''', at 1297 East [[Florida State Road 78|State Road 78]] in remote [[Moore Haven, Florida]], United States, opened in 2007 with 440 beds. Operated by the [[Glades County Sheriff's Office]], besides Glades County arrestees, 90% of its beds house [[Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] detainees, which were previously spread around many county jails. It is [[Glades County]]'s largest employer.<ref>{{cite news
|title=Glades cells to ease Lee crunch
|first=Pat
|last=Gillespie
|newspaper=[[The News-Press]] ([[Fort Myers, Florida]])
|date=15 May 2006
|page=1
|via=[[newspapers.com]]
|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94428006/opening-of-glades-county-detention/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
|title=More than a Jail. Immigrant Detention and the Smell of Money
|first1=Jacob
|last1=Kang-Brown
|first2=Jack
|last2=Norton
|publisher=[[Vera Institute]]
|url=https://www.vera.org/in-our-backyards-stories/glades-county-more-than-a-jail
 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220314/https://www.vera.org/in-our-backyards-stories/glades-county-more-than-a-jail
 |archive-date=2022-03-14 |url-status=live|date=July 5, 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref> It has been the site of widespread abuses, and in 2022, 17 members of Congress asked that it be closed.<ref name=Letter/><ref name=Aclu/>

==2018–2020 complaints==
In 2018, Muslims complained of not being able to observe [[Ramadan]], with Christians, according to them, receiving preferential treatment.<ref>{{citation
|title=Florida ICE Detention Center Restricts Detainees' Observance of Ramadan
|date=October 12, 2018
|first=Steve
|last=Horn
|newspaper=[[Prison Legal News]]
|url=https://www.prisonlegalnews.org/news/2018/oct/12/florida-ice-detention-center-restricts-detainees-observance-ramadan/}}</ref>

In 2019, a group of Muslim inmates filed suit alleging they were denied "adequate prayer services, copies of the [[Quran]], religious headwear, and religiously compliant diets. When asked by one detained immigrant why Muslims were treated so disfavorably, the chaplain replied, 'Boy, you’re in Glades County.'"<ref>{{cite news
|title=Border Patrol and ICE routinely violate immigrants' religious rights
|first=Aleksandr
|last=Sverdlik
|newspaper=[[Independent Coast Observer]] ([[Gualala, California]])
|date=29 Mar 2019
|page=A12
|via=[[newspapers.com]]
|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94438154/lawsuit-by-muslim-inmates-at-glades/}}</ref>

In April 2020, the [[Southern Poverty Law Center]], the Immigration Clinic at the [[University of Miami School of Law]], and other plaintiffs sued the Immigration and Customs Enforcement Agency and the U.S. Attorney General. They sought the release of inmates at Glades and its other south Florida centers, [[Krome Processing Center]] in [[Miami-Dade]] and the [[Broward Transitional Center]] in [[Pompano Beach]], claiming that ICE was not following [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] guidelines to minimize [[COVID-19]] transmission.<ref>{{cite news
|title=Lawsuit. ICE breaks CDC guidelines in S. Fla. detention sites
|newspaper=[[Miami Herald]] ([[Miami, Florida]])
|date=14 Apr 2020
|page=A5
|first=Monique O.
|last=Madan
|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94815984/suing-south-florida-ice-detention-sites/}}</ref> (Other Florida counties whose detention centers have contracts to house ICE detainees are [[Baker County, Florida|Baker]], [[Collier County|Collier]], [[Monroe County, Florida|Monroe]], [[Pinellas County|Pinellas]], and [[Wakulla County|Wakulla]].<ref>{{cite news
|title=Are the kids all right? A patchwork system makes it hard to find details about migrant children in Florida (pg. 2 of 2)
|newspaper=[[Tampa Bay Times]] ([[St. Petersburg, Florida]])
|date=30 Jun 2018
|page=A6
|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94813883/conditions-in-florida-ice-detention/
|first1=Alex
|last1=Leary
|first2=Steve
|last2=Bousquet}}</ref>)

==2021 complaints==
In February 2021, a civil rights complaint, described as "scathing" in a newspaper, was filed by three immigrants' rights organizations with the Inspector General and the Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties in the Department of Homeland Security. Although the Glades County center "has ranked among the nation’s most COVID-riddled detention centers." According to the complaint, masks and COVID-19 tests are not available, temperatures are only taken irregularly, and the center's one doctor had COVID-19 and did not wear a mask. Detainees reporting abuses are punished.<ref>{{cite news
|title='Like sardines in a can': Complaint alleges medical neglect at Florida ICE detention center
|newspaper=[[Miami Herald]] ([[Miami, Florida]])
|date=23 Feb 2021
|page=A4
|first=Monique O.
|last=Madan
|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94937123/conditions-at-glades-county-detention/}}</ref> A civil rights complaint was filed March 4 with the Office of Civil Rights and Civil Liberties under the Department of Homeland Security concerning what were described as retaliatory actions against two of the plaintiffs in the February complaint.<ref>{{cite web
|title=Sheriff's Office Staff at Glades County, Florida, Pepper Spray, Assault, Throw Men Into Solitary Confinement in Retaliation for Complaint
|newspaper=[[Targeted News Service]]
|date=5 March 2021
|via=[[Gale OneFile]]
|url=http://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A653923095/STND
|access-date=14 Feb 2022}}</ref><!--"Violations of Civil Rights, COVID-19 Protocols, Reckless Endangerment, and other Abuses at the Glades County Detention Center".<ref>{{citation
|title=Violations of Civil Rights, COVID-19 Protocols, Reckless Endangerment, and other Abuses at the Glades County Detention Center (Florida)-->

In June 2021, according to Doctors for Camp Closure, "The people held at this immigration detention center report not having access to medical attention, negligence, inadequate physical distancing or masks."<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/opinion/commentary/fl-op-com-glades-county-dentention-center-immigration-20210627-qcexzncxbvcsvisasynxxpmv3q-story.html
 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220314/https://www.sun-sentinel.com/opinion/commentary/fl-op-com-glades-county-dentention-center-immigration-20210627-qcexzncxbvcsvisasynxxpmv3q-story.html
 |archive-date=2022-03-14 |url-status=live|title=Glades County Detention Center should release immigrants
|first=Lorena del Pilar
|last=Bonilla
|newspaper=[[Sun Sentinel]] ([[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]])
|date=June 27, 2021}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

In August 2021, according to ''[[Scientific American]]'', the Glades County facility was not diluting chemicals used for disinfection and COVID-19 prevention according to the manufacturer's directions.<ref>{{cite journal
|title=Immigrants in U.S. Detention Exposed to Hazardous Disinfectants Every Day. The chemical concentrations exceed EPA limits, and new human studies suggest they could do long-term damage
|first=Matthew
|last=Phelan
|date=September 17, 2021
|journal=[[Scientific American]]
|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/immigrants-in-u-s-detention-exposed-to-hazardous-disinfectants-every-day/}}</ref>

In September 2021, about 100 detainees, as did detainees at other facilities,<ref>{{cite news
|title=ICE detainees go on hunger strike to press for COVID-19 protection. More than 2,000 immigrants at ICE facilities in California, Florida, New Mexico, Ohio, and other states have refused meals in protest since March, according to Detention Watch Network, an advocacy group.
|date=September 7, 2020
|first=Farida Jhabvala
|last=Romero
|newspaper=[[The World (radio program)|The World]]
|url=https://theworld.org/stories/2020-09-07/ice-detainees-go-hunger-strike-press-covid-19-protections-0 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220314/https://theworld.org/stories/2020-09-07/ice-detainees-go-hunger-strike-press-covid-19-protections-0 |archive-date=2022-03-14 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref> participated in a [[hunger strike]]. According to inmates who had already been in federal prisons, conditions at Glades were worse.<ref>{{cite news
|title=Civil rights complaint targets Glades ICE facility (part 1 of 2)
|page=3
|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94942122/complaints-about-glades-county/
|newspaper=[[The News-Press]] ([[Fort Myers, Florida]])
|date=18 Sep 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/94942515/glades-county-ice-hunger-strike-pt-2/
|title=Civil rights complaint targets Glades ICE facility (part 2 of 2)
|page=7
|newspaper=[[The News-Press]] ([[Fort Myers, Florida]])
|date=18 Sep 2021}}</ref>

In October 2021, the Inspector General of the Department of Homeland Security, after an audit, reported that the "U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) did not always comply with segregation reporting requirements [COVID-19 segregation] and did not ensure detention facilities complied with records retention requirements."<ref name=Oig>{{cite book
|title=ICE Needs to Improve Its Oversight of Segregation Use in Detention Facilities
|date=October 13, 2021
|author=Office of Inspector General, Department of Homeland Security
|url=https://www.oig.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/assets/2021-10/OIG-22-01-Oct21.pdf
|access-date=February 9, 2021}}</ref>{{rp|1}} According to the report, Congress—where the House of Representatives held a hearing on September 26, 2019—"and the public have expressed concerns regarding prolonged or excessive use of segregation at ICE detention facilities. From FY 2015 through FY 2019, the DHS OIG Hotline received 1,200 allegations related to concerns about segregation."<ref name=Oig/>{{rp|4}}

In November 2021 a coalition of groups wrote the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) requesting that it cancel its contract with Glades County for the Glades County Detention Center (“Glades”) because of what it called a "systemic and consistent pattern of racism and anti-Blackness towards Black immigrants." The groups were the [[American Civil Liberties Union]] of Florida, Americans for Immigrant Justice, Borderless Existence Initiative, Detention Watch Network, Doctors for Camp Closure, Envision Freedom Fund, Freedom for Immigrants, Immigrant Action Alliance, [[Southern Poverty Law Center]], [[University of Miami School of Law]] Immigration Clinic, [[United We Dream]], and Qlatinx. The 157-page document contains numerous sworn statements about misconduct experienced or witnessed.<ref>{{citation
|title=Racism at Glades County Detention Center
|date=November 18, 2021
|author=Shutdown Glades Coalition
|url=https://www.aclufl.org/sites/default/files/field_documents/memo_to_dhs_re_racism_at_glades_detention_center_11.18.21.pdf
|access-date=February 9, 2022}}</ref>

==2022 complaints==
In January 2022, the American Civil Liberties Union of Florida wrote Acting ICE Director [[Tae D. Johnson]] and [[David S. Ferriero]], Archivist of the United States (head of the [[National Archives and Records Administration|National Archives]]), calling for an end to systematic, and in their judgment illegal, erasure of surveillance video at the Glades County facility, in violation of federal recordkeeping law and contractual requjrements.<ref>{{citation
|title=Request for Prompt Remedial Action Regarding Ongoing Deletion of Surveillance Video at ICE Detention Facility
|date=January 24, 2022
|first1=Nikhel S.
|last1=Sus
|first2=Katherine H.
|last2=Blankenship
|url=https://www.citizensforethics.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/2022.01.24-Letter-from-ACLU-FL-CREW-to-ICE-NARA.pdf
|access-date=February 9, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
|title=An ICE detention center in Florida is deleting evidence. It signals a systemic problem
|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/opinion/commentary/fl-op-com-ice-glades-detention-center-20220204-p2nswjjd7rhazcdeiau3xucfzy-story.html
 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220314/https://www.sun-sentinel.com/opinion/commentary/fl-op-com-ice-glades-detention-center-20220204-p2nswjjd7rhazcdeiau3xucfzy-story.html
 |archive-date=2022-03-14 |url-status=live|first1=Nikhel
|last1=Sus
|first2=Katie
|last2=Blankenship
|date=February 4, 2022 
|newspaper=[[Sun Sentinel]] ([[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]])}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

On February 1, 2022, [[Debbie Wasserman Schultz]] and 16 other members of Congress sent a joint letter to [[Alejandro Mayorkas]], Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, pointing out that reports of abuses had increased since their complaint in the summer of 2021, and asking that it be closed. According to their complaint, "immigrants have been subject to racist abuse, often resulting in verbal abuse and violence; sexual abuse, including sexual voyeurism by guards who have watched women shower; life-endangering COVID-19 and medical neglect, including a near-fatal carbon monoxide leak last November; and regular exposure to highly dangerous levels of a toxic disinfectant chemical spray linked to severe medical harms and long-term damage to reproductive health."<ref name=Letter>{{citation
|title=Letter to Alejandro Mayorkas
|date=February 1, 2021
|first1=Debbie
|last1=Wasserman Schultz
|author-link1=Debbie Wasserman Schultz
|author2=and 16 other members of Congress
|url=https://www.scribd.com/document/556459160/Letter-to-Secretary-Mayorkas-Feb-2022
|access-date=February 9, 2021}}</ref><ref name=Aclu>{{cite news
|title=No one should be treated this way: Congressional leaders renew call on Biden administration to close troubled Florida ICE Prison
|first=Jeff
|last=Migliozzi
|access-date=February 14, 2022
|publisher=[[ACLU]] of Florida
|date=February 2, 2022
|url=https://www.aclufl.org/en/press-releases/no-one-should-be-treated-way-congressional-leaders-renew-call-biden-administration |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220314/https://www.aclufl.org/en/press-releases/no-one-should-be-treated-way-congressional-leaders-renew-call-biden-administration |archive-date=2022-03-14 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
